subject: Urgent: BrightBeam RTT & p95/p99 spike — possible cross‑region routing
messages:
From: Amira Hassan <amira@brightbeam.com>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.ai>
Cc: ops@brightbeam.com
Date: 2027-08-12 09:23:00 -0700
Subject: Sudden p95/p99 RTT spike impacting inference in us-west

Hi Evelyn,

We started seeing a large increase in request latency from our production traffic around 08:55 PDT this morning. p95 jumped from ~80ms to ~420ms and p99s are off the charts; error rates are also slightly elevated (0.6% -> 1.8%). This coincides with a regional failover window on our side but we don't see anything on our infra that would explain the path shift to eu endpoints. Can you confirm whether anything changed on Redwood routing or egress mappings?

This is affecting user sessions for two of our largest customers — we need immediate assistance and a short-term mitigation if possible.

Attachments: traces-sample-08-12.json (small), screenshot-p95-0808.png

Regards,
Amira
Head of Platform Engineering, BrightBeam

From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.ai>
To: Amira Hassan <amira@brightbeam.com>
Cc: jonas.weber@redwood.ai, marissa.cole@redwood.ai, sean.gallagher@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-08-12 09:39:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Sudden p95/p99 RTT spike impacting inference in us-west

Amira — thanks for the heads up. I'm escalating to our SRE and CS teams and will coordinate a targeted mitigation.

Immediate plan: I have asked Jonas to pull cross-region traces and traceroutes; if this is an egress-mapping issue we can push a temporary route override to restore the correct us-west path while we investigate root cause. Marissa will follow up with a customer-facing status and rollback/credit guidance.

Expected next update: ~30 minutes with first triage.

– Evelyn
Evelyn Hart
Director, Customer Success — Redwood Inference
[evelyn.hart@redwood.ai]

From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.ai>, marissa.cole@redwood.ai
Cc: sean.gallagher@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-08-12 10:01:12 -0700
Subject: Re: Sudden p95/p99 RTT spike impacting inference in us-west

Quick triage notes:
- Pulled distributed traces and active traceroutes for BrightBeam consumer IP blocks.
- Observed that a subset of requests originating in us-west are being routed through our eu-west egress node (latency delta ~320–550ms).
- Prelim diff of recent config push shows a mis-applied egress mapping change: svc-egress-map for traffic tagged "bb-prod-us" lost the region-specific match and fell back to the default path. See attached patch (svc-egress-mapping-diff.patch) showing the unintended removal.
- No sign of degraded compute on inference fleets; root cause appears network-routing/egress mapping.

Immediate mitigation applied: re-inserted the us-west region match and force-warmed the route table for the affected backend pools. I've also pushed a temporary policy to prefer local egress for traffic with the BrightBeam tag. Early metrics show p95 falling back toward baseline (current p95 ~140ms and trending down).

Next: will keep route pinned for 2 hours while we validate stability, then prepare a config rollback with a safer deploy path (canary + verification) and postmortem.

Attachments: brightbeam-traces-2027-08-12.tar.gz
– Jonas

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Amira Hassan <amira@brightbeam.com>
Cc: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.ai>, jonas.weber@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-08-12 10:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Sudden p95/p99 RTT spike impacting inference in us-west

Hi Amira —

Thank you for flagging this and for the traces. Jonas pushed a targeted fix to restore the us-west egress mapping about 10 minutes ago; our monitoring shows p95 improving but we want to validate over a longer window to be sure.

What we're doing for BrightBeam right now:
- Route override pinned for 2 hours and health-checked every 5m.
- Rolling canary to ensure the change won't affect other tenants.
- Preparing a formal postmortem and a plan to change our deploy gating to catch egress-map regressions.

Tactical offer: we can apply a short credit for the affected window and prioritize a configuration hardening rollout for BrightBeam. I'll follow up with a proposal for credit amount and timeline by EOD.

Apologies for the disruption — we'll get this stabilized and follow up with a detailed timeline.

Best,
Marissa
Senior Customer Success Manager, Redwood Inference

Recommended immediate items:
- Approve a goodwill credit up to $12k for the impacted window and expedite postmortem review.
- Consider a targeted configuration-gating task to add a pre-deploy egress-map validation check (this should be a high-priority infra ticket).

If approved I'll thread a concise executive note to BrightBeam CTO and include the remediation timeline and credit offer.

– Sean
VP, Sales — Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Amira Hassan <amira@brightbeam.com>, Amira Hassan <amiracopy@brightbeam.com>
Cc: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.ai>, jonas.weber@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-08-14 17:10:00 -0700
Subject: BrightBeam incident wrap-up and next steps

Hi Amira — apologies again for the disruption on Thursday. We completed a full validation and can confirm the regression was due to a misapplied egress‑mapping change that caused a subset of us-west traffic to route via eu-west egress nodes.

What we did:
- Immediate route override on 2027-08-12 10:00 PDT to restore correct us-west paths (p95 returned toward baseline within ~12 minutes).
- Full configuration rollback and a new canary gating workflow to prevent similar regressions.
- Postmortem draft attached and a set of suggested deploy checks for egress-mapping (see postmortem-draft.md).

Compensation: as discussed, we're issuing a $10,500 service credit for the impacted window and offering a follow-up technical session with our SRE team to walk through the new gating checks.

We'll schedule the session for next week — please let me know preferred times.

Thanks for your patience — we take reliability seriously and appreciate your partnership.

Best,
Marissa
Senior Customer Success Manager, Redwood Inference
Attachments: postmortem-draft.md
